text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended slightly lower due to pre-weekend profit-taking. Turnover was a mere 4,872 lots and the bulk of business was in spread trading. July lost $2 to close at $1,840 per tonne, while September gave up $4 to close at $1,856 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York ended mixed in thin, choppy trade as light speculative selling was offset by trade buying toward the lows. Continued mild weather in Brazil undermined sentiment. Traders said conditions in Brazil are generally favourable for the trees but some disruptions to the harvest are still expected from scattered showers. July added 3.05 cents/lb to close at 198.95 cents/lb. September gave up 35 points to close at 179.50 cents/lb. Lower differentials for the front months have stimulated demand, traders said.

COLOMBIA - John Naranjo, commercial manager of Colombia's National Coffee Growers Federation, said that 1997/98 production (October/September) should be around 12 million bags. He added that the Federation was baffled by an earlier statement from the London-based Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) pegging Colombia's 1997/98 crop at up to 15 million bags. However, the ACPC said that its estimate of the Colombian 1997/98 crop is between 12.0 and 12.5 million bags and that the figure of 15 million bags has never been mentioned. USDA recently estimated the 1997/98 crop at 11.3 million bags. Naranjo gave no fresh estimate for 1996/97. Earlier reports said that the crop in that year would be 10 million bags.

**PERU - According to the Junta Nacional de Cafe, exportable production in 1996/97 (April/March) reached 1.450 million 60-bags, up from 1.324 million bags produced the previous year. However, it is feared that production in 1997/98 may be significantly down due to the El Nino weather system. The country has recently declared nine of its 24 regions in emergency to speed the nation's preparations for the harmful 'El Nino' that is expected to form later this year. The weather phenomenon causes droughts in the south of Peru and heavy rainfalls in the country's north.

**POLAND - Poland imported 123,591 bags of coffee in February 1997, only little changed from the 123,383 bags imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports in the first two months of 1997 up to 285,665 bags, 5 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/February 1997 were Uganda (35,400 vs 9,100 bags), Indonesia (73,000 vs 46,900 bags) and Vietnam (50,800 vs 44,600 bags). The country exported 18,200 bags of coffee in January/February 1997, up from 9,800 bags exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose to 88,200 bags, up from 42,300 bags in 1995.
